title: Cleanliness and personal hygiene
intro: Cleanliness is half of faith – and, doctors say, half of health.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah loves those who turn to Him often in repentance, and He loves those who keep themselves clean. <small>(Qur’an, Al-Baqarah 2:222)</small>

Following this ayah, every Muslim must keep the body, clothes and place where they live clean. Cleanliness is a condition for all the Islamic duties – from the Shahadah, Salah and fasting to zakah and Hajj.
To keep our body, clothes and home clean, we keep away from the main kinds of impurity (najasah): alcohol, blood, pus, urine, stool and anything else that comes out of a human or animal body.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: Muhammad (SAW) said: “Cleanliness is half of faith.” (Muslim) And medicine says that cleanliness is half of health.

items: every morning after getting up, making wudu or washing the face and brushing the teeth
always washing the hands before and after eating
cleaning ourselves after using the toilet, and washing the hands with soap
brushing the teeth well after every meal

learn.html: We also keep our yard clean and tidy, with green grass and many flowers.

learn.title: 💬 Imam Abu Hanifah’s story
learn.html: Imam Abu Hanifah was always neat, nicely dressed and smelled good. One day he saw a man sitting with him in old, worn clothes. Later he gave him a thousand dirhams to look after his appearance. The man said: “I am rich – I don’t need sadaqah.” Abu Hanifah said: “Haven’t you heard the hadith: ‘Allah loves to see the trace of His blessing on His servant’? Change your appearance, so your friend does not have to hide from you.”

practice.title: A clean day
items: Wake up and make wudu or wash
Put on clean clothes for the next day
